blocking_unknown: Every registration path freezes, including the cleanest. In-place overwrite of a same-type header-table record (0x3EDEFC) with no shift and unchanged file length loaded with the ORIGINAL spawn fully constructed, yet still hung on Loading with the clone absent from RAM. So registering a same-type record in a valid slot is necessary but NOT sufficient: duplicating a type-92 spawn-owner entity is blocked by a deeper construction constraint that in-place single-field mutation (M2, PASS) never triggers — a candidate is the type-92 construction iterating its children by blob/count and mis-parsing the zeroed leftover, or a duplicated record conflicting on an identity/handle/dependency. Duplicating this entity is not achievable with byte-level file editing at the current understanding. Relocation itself is reflection-driven (no flat table to extend; finding igz.loader.relocation-table).

mechanism_found: Why a valid appended IGZ object is not instantiated: (1) the loader does not walk section 1 sequentially, does not use the header table as a construction root and does not use the section-0 table as a size stream; it constructs a contiguous span of records and each record builds its embedded children (findings igz.loader.enumerated-span, igz.loader.pointer-traversal). (2) An object appended after the last record is outside the span and stays raw bytes (never constructed) — the cause of the first M3 failure. (3) Loading applies a fixup pass: section-indexed pointers (igz.pointer.section-indexed), class pointers, id remap, reference counts (igz.object.refcount); section 5 is a second object section with 2 320 pointers into section 1 (igz.section5.object-section).
